description: Four ambitious minds. One shared vision. We are a team of dreamers, builders, and future leaders who believe that extraordinary things start with bold ideas and the courage to pursue them. We think beyond limits, challenge the ordinary, and turn possibilities into reality. Our goal isn't just to dream big — it's to build something meaningful that makes a difference.
summary:
FLAMMA SI is a web dashboard that turns NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive into answers for fire safety in crewed habitats. On Earth, flames rise. In microgravity they behave very differently, and the evidence is spread across 24 investigations, nearly two thousand tests and dozens of papers that are hard to find, compare and understand.

We pulled every combustion investigation into one structured Atlas: objective, fuel, oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity, variables and measurements. Users pick a habitat (Moon base, Mars base or spacecraft cabin) and see how ready the evidence is for prevention, detection, suppression and gravity effects. They can then rank investigations, compare them side by side, explore the raw test data in the Data Lab, and download any view as PDF, Excel or CSV.

FLAMMA, our AI guide, answers questions with charts and citations to the PSI records, at student or researcher level, in English and Russian. It can also generate a short video briefing.

This matters because fire is one of the biggest risks on long missions. FLAMMA SI helps engineers, researchers and students see what NASA has already tested, and where the gaps remain.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NASA has run 24 combustion investigations in microgravity: more than 2,000 tests, written up in 352 publications. It's an amazing archive, but it's hard to use. The data sits in PDFs, spreadsheets and papers, and if you're designing a Moon base, you don't have weeks to dig through it.

So we built FLAMMA SI. You pick a habitat (the ISS, a spacecraft cabin, a Moon base, a pressurized rover, a Mars base, or Earth for reference), and the whole dashboard adapts to it. Every page answers the same three questions for that place: how would a fire start and spread, how would we spot it, and how would we put it out?

HOW IT WORKS

The Overview shows the habitat's gravity, oxygen and pressure, with a 3D combustion chamber and a live flame in the middle. Below it, four verdicts (Prevention, Detection, Suppression and Gravity) tell you how strong the evidence is, and each one links to the experiments behind it.

From there you can dig in. The Ranker scores every investigation with a formula you can see and adjust. The Atlas has a card for each experiment: what was burned, at what oxygen, pressure and airflow, what changed between tests, and what they found. Compare puts two to four experiments side by side and highlights what they share. The Data Lab opens the raw test tables, and Equipment & Earth shows seven fire-safety technologies plus how this research helps on Earth, from smoke detectors to firefighter gear. Anything you find can be downloaded as a PDF, an Excel file or a CSV.

Then there's FLAMMA, our flame-shaped guide. Ask it anything about the data and it answers in seconds, cites the exact NASA record behind every fact, and draws a chart when that helps. It speaks English and Russian, can explain things simply or technically, and can turn any answer into a short narrated video.

WHY IT MATTERS

Fire is one of the most serious risks on a long mission, and in microgravity it doesn't behave the way it does on Earth. The research to understand it already exists. FLAMMA SI makes it usable: engineers can check what's been tested for their exact conditions, researchers can decide where to go next, and students can finally see why a flame in space is round and blue instead of tall and orange.

HOW WE BUILT IT

The frontend is React 19 with TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS. We used ECharts for the charts, React Three Fiber for the 3D chamber, ExcelJS and pdfmake for the downloads, and the browser's own speech engine for the narration. The backend runs as serverless functions on Vercel. A Python pipeline turns the PSI records and test tables into clean, structured data. FLAMMA's answers come from the DeepSeek model, which is given the full NASA knowledge base with every request, plus tools that quote individual test rows exactly.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT

We wanted this to feel friendly, not like a spreadsheet. FLAMMA is a hand-traced, animated character: it blinks, thinks, talks, and gives new users a quick tour. Switching habitats changes everything at once, from the cabin around the 3D chamber to every chart and verdict, so you really feel the difference between the ISS and the Moon.

WHAT WE CARED ABOUT

Trust came first. Every number, ranking, verdict and chart is calculated straight from NASA's data by fixed rules, not by AI, and FLAMMA has to cite a source for every fact it states. We also built for two audiences, students and researchers, in two languages. We kept the scope on habitat fires, so rocket and propellant fires are not covered.

USE OF AI

The code was written with Claude Code (Anthropic). Inside the app, DeepSeek writes FLAMMA's answers, comparisons, briefings and video scripts, and it wrote the English and Russian summaries of each investigation from the NASA records. All the numbers come straight from the data. The data is from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), released under CC0.
